definition: A confusion network (sometimes called a word confusion network or informally known as a sausage) is a natural language processing method that combines outputs from multiple automatic speech recognition or machine translation systems.
details: Confusion networks are simple linear directed acyclic graphs with the property that each a path from the start node to the end node goes through all the other nodes. The set of words represented by edges between two nodes is called a confusion set. In machine translation, the defining characteristic of confusion networks is that they allow multiple ambiguous inputs, deferring committal translation decisions until later stages of processing. This approach is used in the open source machine translation software Moses and the proprietary translation API in IBM Bluemix Watson.

explainer.lead: A confusion network keeps several possible words in play instead of forcing a speech recognizer or translator to choose too early. It packs alternatives into a simple graph, letting a later processing stage select one complete result.

tiers.eli5: It's like lining up several people's transcripts of the same sentence side by side, so you can pick the best word at each spot later instead of guessing right away.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers build linear directed acyclic graphs whose paths pass through all nodes, with each edge set between two nodes forming a confusion set. A pitfall is committing to a translation too early rather than deferring it.
tiers.paperLevel: A simple linear directed acyclic graph in which every path from start to end node passes through all other nodes; the words on edges between two nodes form a confusion set. Its defining property in MT is allowing multiple ambiguous inputs, with limits set by the graph's linear structure.

components.name: Start and end nodes
components.detail: Mark the boundaries of every complete hypothesis represented by the network.

components.name: Ordered intermediate nodes
components.detail: Fix the sequence of positions through which every complete path must pass.

components.name: Confusion sets
components.detail: Groups of word-bearing edges between two nodes hold the alternatives for one position.

components.name: Complete paths
components.detail: Each path from start to end selects one word alternative at every position.

flow: Multiple speech-recognition or translation outputs supply alternative words.
The alternatives are placed on edges between successive nodes as confusion sets.
Later processing considers complete start-to-end paths instead of receiving one early, fixed choice.
For example, a confusion set containing “there” and “their” preserves both options until a complete path is selected.
explainer.whyItMatters: It provides a compact way to preserve ambiguity and combine system outputs. Deferring commitments gives later stages more than one hypothesis to work with.
